questions.q: Why is an oversized gradient step more dangerous in policy optimization than in ordinary supervised learning?
options: It isn't more dangerous; the two cases are identical
A bad policy update can shift behavior so much that subsequent experience is qualitatively worse, with no guaranteed path back
Policy networks cannot use gradient descent at all
Supervised learning never uses gradients
questions.explain: Unlike supervised learning where the next batch is just a noisier version of before, a bad policy update changes what experience gets collected next, potentially degrading the policy irrecoverably.

questions.q: What does the probability ratio pi_theta(a|s) / pi_theta_old(a|s) in the TRPO surrogate objective represent?
options: The discount factor applied to future rewards
How much more or less likely the new policy is to take an action than the old policy was
The replay buffer's sampling probability
The KL-divergence between two policies
questions.explain: The ratio directly compares the new policy's probability of an action to the old policy's probability of the same action, forming the basis of the importance-sampled surrogate objective.

questions.q: What does TRPO's KL-divergence constraint limit?
options: The number of training steps allowed
How much the new policy's output distribution is allowed to differ from the old policy's, measured behaviorally rather than in parameter space
The size of the replay buffer
The number of actions available to the agent
questions.explain: TRPO constrains the KL-divergence between old and new action distributions, which measures a behavioral change in the policy — not simply how far the parameters theta moved.

questions.q: Why does TRPO use a surrogate objective instead of directly maximizing expected return?
options: Because expected return cannot be estimated at all
Because the surrogate, built from probability ratios and advantage, is much cheaper to evaluate and a good local approximation near the old policy
Because the surrogate objective requires no advantage estimates
Because expected return is always negative
questions.explain: Directly maximizing true expected return is expensive and high-variance to evaluate; the probability-ratio surrogate is a tractable, data-reusable approximation that holds well close to the old policy.

questions.q: Why is TRPO rarely used directly in practice today, despite being foundational?
options: It performs worse than random policies
Solving its constrained optimization exactly requires conjugate gradients and curvature approximations, which are expensive and intricate to implement correctly
It cannot be applied to any RL problem
It requires no advantage function at all
questions.explain: TRPO's exact solution needs second-order curvature approximations, Fisher-information-matrix-vector products, and conjugate gradient solves — complex machinery that PPO largely avoids while keeping similar safety properties.
